slot.brief: Identify hybridisation/shape of xenon fluoride molecule (XeF4/XeF6) or similar hypervalent species using VSEPR; simple counting with lone-pair placement.

stem: According to VSEPR theory, what are the number of lone pairs on xenon and the shape of $\text{XeF}_4$?

verdicts.working: XeF₄ has four bonding pairs and two lone pairs on Xe (AX₄E₂), giving a square-planar molecular shape.

working:
Xe has $8$ valence electrons; four Xe–F bonds leave two lone pairs on Xe. The six electron pairs are octahedral, with the two lone pairs opposite; the molecular shape is square planar.

Independent check: XeF₄ has four bonding pairs and two lone pairs on Xe (AX₄E₂), giving a square-planar molecular shape.
